subject: Discovery recap — semantic search + rerank: index scale, SLA targets, next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@searchly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — semantic search + rerank: index scale, SLA targets, next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Tail latency spikes during peak hours causing a bad UX for enterprise customers (slow periods ~95th > 400ms).
- Cost per query is high due to a large candidate set + cross-encoder rerank stage.
- Operational overhead running Milvus + custom GPU fleet for reranking (want to reduce infra ops).

2) Current stack and signals you gave
- Vector store: Milvus on K8s with 95M vectors, 1536-d float embeddings, product index ~120GB (quantized).
- Rerank: cross-encoder (BERT-like) run as a separate GPU service; candidate set size today ~100; average qps ~400 with spikes to ~1,200.
- Ingestion: nightly bulk batch (ETL) + nearline updates for hot docs.

3) Success criteria you care about (we heard)
- 95th percentile latency for online queries < 120ms (target; hard SLO for end-users).
- Reduce cost per routed query by ~3x (ops + infra).
- Drop operational overhead and remove pain of managing GPU cluster for rerank.

4) Redwood-fit observations (from our side)
- We can evaluate a two-stage pipeline: lightweight ANN retrieval (quantized index, contiguous memory) + Redwood-hosted rerank using a small cross-encoder tuned for latency.
- Options: Hosted API for quick PoC; Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and cost at scale; Private if you need VPC/on-prem later.

5) Immediate next steps (proposed)
- You to send a small index snapshot + sample queries and query latency histogram (attached CSV looks great) — we requested prod_index_snapshot_20260520.csv.
- Redwood to run a scoped benchmark (ANN recall/latency + rerank cost) on a 10M vector subset and share a cost/latency matrix.
- Schedule architecture review with your infra and ML lead to map integration points and auth/KMS needs. Suggested: Mon/Tue next week.
- Share any compliance constraints (data residency, SOC 2 evidence needed) if relevant.

Attachments: prod_index_snapshot_20260520.csv (you uploaded during the call), current_query_costs.xlsx (optional, you said you'd share).

If that all looks right, we'll spin up the benchmark and confirm a meeting time.

Thanks — Soojin
--

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — semantic search + rerank: index scale, SLA targets, next steps

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications and additions:

- Index size: earlier I rounded up — the active product index we care about is ~95M vectors (the 120GB number is after replication and secondary indices).
- Candidate set: historically we've used 100 candidates, but the team has been experimenting with 200 for recall-sensitive queries.
- QPS: steady-state ~400 QPS with a 09:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:00 peak windows where we see ~1,000–1,200 QPS for short bursts (~5–10 minutes).
- Rerank infra: currently we run a small GPU fleet (8x V100s) and it’s expensive to operate — main goal is to reduce that burden.

We attached the query cost workbook and a quick latency histogram. Also, two non-functional requirements:
- Data cannot leave US regions for now.
- We need a demo of a 95th percentile SLA before we sign up for Dedicated.

We can do Monday or Tuesday afternoons — prefer Mon 14:00 PT if that works for your team.

On the attachments: current_query_costs.xlsx (contains cost by component and sample billing month).

Alex
